Here we have two variables, $x$ and $y.$ We will start by grouping the two variables separately: 

$$
\begin{aligned}x({x}^{3}{y}^{5})({x}^{2}{y}^{9}) & = \\ {x}^{1}\cdot {x}^{3}\cdot {y}^{5}\cdot {x}^{2}\cdot {y}^{9} & = \\ ({x}^{1}\cdot {x}^{3}\cdot {x}^{2})({y}^{5}\cdot {y}^{9})\end{aligned}
$$

This way, we can apply the product rule to the two variables independently:

$$
\begin{aligned}({x}^{1}\cdot {x}^{3}\cdot {x}^{2})({y}^{5}\cdot {y}^{9}) & = \\ {x}^{(1+3+2)}\cdot {y}^{(5+9)} & = \\ {x}^{6}{y}^{14}\end{aligned}
$$
